meta: Tank failed or flooding the garage? We shut it down, swap the unit and restore hot water in Oakley, CA. Clear price before work starts. Call (888) 910-8644.
lead: Emergency water heater replacement in Oakley, CA for a tank that has failed, flooded a garage or closet, or left the house cold.
We size the new unit, set it, strap it and test it, with a clear price before work starts.
intro: Water heater replacement means removing a failed tank (or an unrepairable tankless unit) and setting a new one in its place, connected to your water, gas or power, venting and drain. In Oakley, CA that usually happens in a garage, utility closet or side yard, and it often starts with a puddle at the base.
This page covers what to do first, how to tell a dead tank from a fixable one, which type to choose, the local rules that touch a swap in Contra Costa County, and what drives the final price.

sections.h2: Tank leaking or flooding right now
paras: A tank that leaks from the base or seams is finished, and the water will keep coming until the supply is closed. Our 24/7 emergency dispatch takes these calls at any hour, and the steps below limit the damage while you wait.
Water that reaches drywall, flooring or a stored box in a garage gets worse by the hour, so act before you phone anyone.
do_now: Close the cold water shutoff on the pipe above the heater by turning the handle until it stops.
Turn the power off at the breaker for an electric unit, or set a gas unit's control to off or pilot.
If the closet or garage smells of gas while the tank is failing, walk away from it and call 911 and PG&E at 1-800-743-5000 before dispatch.
Open one hot faucet so the lines can vent, and attach a hose to the drain valve only if the water is not scalding.
Move boxes, tools and electronics out of the wet area, and photograph the water and the label for your insurer.

sections.h2: Signs the tank is past saving
paras: Not every problem means a new heater. These are the signs that point toward replacement rather than a repair bill that will not last.

items.d: Moisture seeping from the shell or the bottom seam means the steel liner has let go. No valve or fitting swap fixes that.
Orange or brown hot water with clear cold water suggests the inside of the tank is corroding.

Sediment baked onto the bottom makes the tank knock as it heats and wastes fuel. Diablo Water District reports an average hardness of 124 mg/L, so mineral buildup is a normal outcome of years of heating.
When a second or third part fails in a short stretch, the tank is usually wearing out as a whole.

items.t: Age of ten years or more
items.d: Check the date code on the rating label. A tank well past a decade that has stopped heating is rarely worth a new element or gas valve.

sections.h2: Tank, tankless or heat pump: picking the replacement
paras: You can usually put back what was there, but a failed unit is also the moment to reconsider. The table keeps the choice to what changes in your house.
If you want the on-demand route, the details are on our [[tankless-water-heater|tankless water heater]] page.

sections.h2: Local rules that touch a swap in Oakley
paras: Gas tanks in the Bay Area fall under Air District rules. Your current heater is not affected by the Air District's zero-NOx rule, which targets the replacement unit and was moved from January 2027 to January 2028 on November 4, 2026.
The same amendments add exemptions, so read the rule text at baaqmd.gov before you buy a gas unit.

Every replacement and new tank also has to be braced or strapped against earthquake movement under Health and Safety Code 19211, which is why the strapping kit is part of the job. The City sets permit scope for swaps, so call the Building Division at 925-625-7005 and describe the old and new unit.

sections.h2: What sets the price of a replacement
paras: Two houses with the same tank size can get very different totals. The price depends on what the old setup needs before the new unit can go in.

factors.d: A larger tank, a tankless unit or a heat pump each cost more than a basic tank of standard size, and the unit itself is the biggest line.
Changing from gas to electric, or the reverse, adds gas line, venting or circuit work.
Worn flue pipe, missing drain pans, a lacking expansion tank or an unsafe shutoff may need to be brought up to the California Plumbing Code.
Attic placement, tight closets and hauling the old tank away change the labor.
Corroded shutoffs or leaking supply lines found when the old unit comes out add repair time. For flooded floors, ask about our [[leak-detection|leak detection]] service.

sections.insurance: Sudden and accidental water damage, such as a tank bursting overnight, is often treated differently by insurers than gradual wear or a slow leak. Ask your insurer before work starts, and keep photos of the tank, the water and the damage.
sections.call_line: Call (888) 910-8644 and we will give you a clear price before work starts.

paras: We start by confirming the failure and the fuel, then drain and remove the old tank. The new unit is set on a pan where space allows, connected with fresh flex lines and shutoffs, and strapped to the wall framing.

Gas units get a vent and leak check before lighting, and electric units are tested at the breaker. We run hot water at the farthest tap to clear air, then show you the shutoff, the temperature setting and the relief valve discharge line.
Homeowners in larger newer houses, such as those in [[plumber-summer-lake-oakley-ca|Summer Lake]], can read how household size shapes the choice of heater.

sections.h2: Before you decide between replacing and repairing
paras: If the tank is dry and the trouble is a pilot, thermostat or element, a fix may be enough, and our [[water-heater-repair|water heater repair]] page explains those cases. If the tank is wet, the choice is already made.

Starting from scratch with a new build or a planned upgrade is a different job, covered under [[water-heater-installation|water heater installation]]. For neighbors in the next town, the same service reaches [[plumber-brentwood-ca|Brentwood]] as well.

faqs.q: Is a leaking water heater an emergency?
a: Yes, if water is spreading or the leak is from the tank body. Shut the cold water and power or gas off, then call. A small drip at a fitting is less urgent, but it can still be a sign of a failing tank.

faqs.q: Do you handle water heater replacement emergencies at night or on weekends in Oakley?
a: Yes. The line is staffed through the night, and a tank that is not yet leaking can sometimes be swapped the same day. Call (888) 910-8644 and tell us whether the unit is gas or electric and where it sits.

faqs.q: Should I repair or replace an old tank?
a: A tank that leaks from the shell cannot be repaired. If it only fails to heat, the age and condition of the tank decide it, and a diagnosis tells you which way to go.

faqs.q: How long does a replacement take?
a: A like-for-like tank is commonly a half-day job when parts are on hand. Tankless and heat pump changes take longer because of venting, gas or electrical work.

faqs.q: Can I replace my gas tank with a heat pump model?
a: Often yes, if there is room, airflow, a condensate path and a 240-volt circuit. We check those before quoting. Ask your electric provider about incentives, and check baaqmd.gov for how the Air District rule is progressing.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a water heater swap in Oakley?
a: Phone the City Building Division before the work and ask what a same-size swap requires. The applicant can be the owner or the installing contractor, and the permit counter is at 3231 Main Street.

faqs.q: What happens to the water after a heater floods a garage?
a: Pull wet items out, run fans, and photograph everything for your insurer. Drywall and insulation that stayed wet for a day or more may need removal, and we do not assess mold or health effects.

cta_mid: A dead tank does not get better by waiting, so tell us what failed and we will plan the swap around your closet and fuel.
cta_end: Get the leak stopped, the old tank out and hot water running again before the next load of laundry piles up.
